newsitem.title: USA: SEC gets $3 million judgment in Motel 6 case.
newsitem.headline: SEC gets $3 million judgment in Motel 6 case.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday it has won a judgment of more than $3 million against a man who traded on confidential information in the Motel 6 insider trader scheme that involved the largest number of defendants accused of this type of fraud.

The SEC has accused more than 25 people in the coast-to- coast insider trading ring that profited off shares of Motel 6 when it was a takeover target in 1990. This is the largest number of people ever charged by the SEC in one insider trading scheme. In addition to the civil suits brought by the SEC, at least six people have been named in criminal cases.

Dallas-based Motel 6, a nationwide chain of economy motels, was acquired by Accor S.A., a French hotel and tourism Company in August 1990. Prior to the takeover, Wall Street buyout firm Kohlberg, Kravis, Roberts & Co. owned the majority stake in Motel 6 through various partnerships.
The SEC said it recently won judgments and settlements involving five defendants who had been tipped off about the takeover.
The largest judgment was against Ira Gorman who was ordered to pay a civil penalty of $2.15 million; to disgorge illegal profits of $717,233 and pay prejudgment interest of $519,634.
